book.title: Rig Veda
book.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
book.license: Public domain translation (Griffith, 1896); transcription from Wikisource. Griffith’s commentary and notes are not included.
book.notes: Complete translation in Griffith’s arrangement: ten Maṇḍalas, one chapter per hymn, one verse per stanza. The Sanskrit text and Griffith’s commentary are not included. Hymn 1.179, which the 1896 edition prints only as an appendix note, is absent.

verses.translation: MAY Agni, yielding to our prayer, the Raksas-slayer, drive away The malady of evil name that hath beset thy labouring womb.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Agni, concurring in the prayer, drive off the eater of the flesh, The malady of evil name that hath attacked thy babe and womb.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That which destroys the sinking germ, the settled, moving embryo, That which will kill the babe at birth, even this will we drive far away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That which divides thy legs that it may lie between the married pair, That penetrates and licks thy side, even this will we exterminate.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: What rests by thee in borrowed form of brother, lover, or of lord, And would destroy thy Progeny, even this will we exterminate.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That which through sleep or darkness hath deceived thee and lies down by thee, And will destroy thy progeny, even this will we exterminate.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FROM both thy nostrils, from thine eyes, from both thine ears and from thy chin, Forth from thy head and brain and tongue I drive thy malady away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From the neck-tendons and the neck, from the breast-bones and from the spine, From shoulders, upper, lower arms, I drive thy malady away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From viscera and all within, forth from the rectum, from the heart, From kidneys, liver, and from spleen, I drive thy malady away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From thighs, from knee-caps, and from heels, and from the forepart of the feet, From hips from stomach, and from groin I drive thy malady away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From what is voided from within, and from thy hair, and from they nails, From all thyself from top to toe, I drive thy malady away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From every member, every hair, disease that comes in every joint, From all thyself, from top to toe, I drive thy malady away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: AVAUNT, thou Master of the mind Depart, and vanish far away. Look on Destruction far from hence. The live man's mind is manifold.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: A happy boon do men elect, a mighty blessing they obtain. Bliss with Vaivasvata they see. The live man's mind seeks many a place.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: If by address, by blame, by imprecation we have committed sin, awake or sleeping, All hateful acts of ours, all evil doings may Agni bear away to distant places.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: When, Indra, Brahmanaspati, our deeds are wrongful and unjust, May provident Angirasa prevent our foes from troubling, us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: We have prevailed this day and won: we are made free from sin and guilt. Ill thoughts, that visit us awake or sleeping, seize the man we hate, yea, seize the man who hateth us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GODS, whatsoe'er the Dove came hither seeking, sent to us as the envoy of Destruction, For that let us sing hymns and make atonement. Well be it with our quadrupeds and bipeds.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Auspicious be the Dove that hath been sent us, a harmless bird, ye Gods, within our dwelling. May Agni, Sage, be pleased with our oblation, and may the Missile borne on wings avoid us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let not the Arrow that hath wings distract us: beside the fire-place, on the hearth it settles. May it bring welfare to our men and cattle: here let the Dove, ye Gods, forbear to harm us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The screeching of the owl is ineffective and when beside the fire the Dove hath settled, To him who sent it hither as an envoy, to him be reverence paid, to Death, to Yama.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Drive forth the Dove, chase it with holy verses: rejoicing, bring ye hither food and cattle, Barring the way against all grief and trouble. Let the swift bird fly forth and leave us vigour.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAKE me a bull among my peers, make me my rivals, conqueror: Make me the slayer of my foes, a sovran ruler, lord of kine
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I am my rivals' slayer, like Indra unwounded and unhurt, And all these enemies of mine are vanquished and beneath my feet.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Here, verily, I bind you fast, as the two bow-ends with the string. Press down these men, O Lord of Speech, that they may humbly speak to me.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Hither I came as conqueror with mighty all-effecting power, And I have mastered all your thought, your synod, and your holy work.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May I be highest, having gained your strength in war, your skill in peace my feet have trodden on your heads. Speak to me from beneath my feet, as frogs from out the water croak, as frogs from out the water croak.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS pleasant meath, O Indra, is effused for thee: thou art the ruling Lord of beaker and of juice. Bestow upon us wealth with many hero sons: thou, having glowed with Fervour, worthest heavenly light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Let us call Sakra to libations here effused, winner of light who joyeth in the potent juice. Mark well this sacrifice of ours and come to us: we pray to Maghavan the Vanquisher of hosts.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: By royal Soma's and by Varuna's decree, under Brhaspati's and Anumati's guard, This day by thine authority, O Maghavan, Maker, Disposer thou! have I enjoyed the jars.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: 1, too, urged on, have had my portion, in the bowl, and as first Prince I drew forth this my hymn of praise, When with the prize I came unto the flowing juice, O Visvamitra, Jamadagni, to your home.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O THE Wind's chariot, O its power and glory! Crashing it goes and hath a voice of thunder. It makes the regions red and touches heaven, and as it moves the dust of earth is scattered.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Along the traces of the Wind they hurry, they come to him as dames to an assembly. Borne on his car with these for his attendants, the God speeds forth, the universe's Monarch.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Travelling on the paths of air's mid region, no single day doth he take rest or slumber. Holy and earliest-born, Friend of the waters, where did he spring and from what region came he?
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Germ of the world, the Deities' vital spirit, this God moves ever as his will inclines him. His voice is heard, his shape is ever viewless. Let us adore this Wind with our oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY the wind blow upon our Cows with healing: may they eat herbage full of vigorous juices. May they drink waters rich in life and fatness: to food that moves on feet be gracious, Rudra.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like-coloured, various-hued, or single-coloured, whose names through sacrifice are known to Agni, Whom the Angirases produced by Fervour, vouchsafe to these, Parjanya, great protection.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Those who have offered to the Gods their bodies, whose varied forms are all well known to Soma,- Those grant us in our cattle-pen, O Indra, with their full streams of milk and plenteous offspring.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Prajapati, bestowing these upon me, one-minded with all Gods and with the Fathers, Hath to our cow-pen brought auspicious cattle: so may we own the offspring they will bear us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY the Bright God drink glorious Soma-mingled meath, giving the sacrifice's lord uninjured life; He who, wind-urged, in person guards our offspring well, hath nourished them with food and shines o'er many a land.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Radiant, as high Truth, cherished, best at winning strength, Truth based upon the statute that supports the heavens, He rose, a light, that kills Vrtras and enemies, best slayer of the Dasyus, Asuras, and foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This light, the best of lights, supreme, all-conquering, winner of riches, is exalted with high laud. All-lighting, radiant, mighty as the Sun to see, he spreadeth wide unfailing victory and strength.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Beaming forth splendour with thy light, thou hast attained heaven's lustrous realm. By thee were brought together all existing things, possessor of all Godhead, All-effecting God.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FOR Ita's sake who pressed the juice, thou, Indra, didst protect his car, And hear the Soma-giver's call.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou from his skin hast borne the head of the swift-moving combatant, And sought the Soma-pourer's home.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Venya, that mortal man, hast thou, for Astrabudhna the devout, O Indra, many a time set free.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring, Indra, to the east again that Sun who now is in the west, Even against the will of Gods.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH all thy beauty come: the kine approaching with full udders follow on thy path.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Come with kind thoughts, most liberal, rousing the warrior's hymn of praise, with bounteous ones,
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As nourishers we tie the thread, and, liberal with our bounty, offer sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dawn drives away her Sister's gloom, and, through her excellence, makes her retrace her path.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BE with us; I have chosen thee: stand steadfast and immovable. Let all the people wish for thee let not thy kingship fall away.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Be even here; fall not away be like a mountain unremoved. Stand steadfast here like Indra's self, and hold the kingship in the grasp.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This man hath Indra stablished, made secure by strong oblation's power. May Soma speak a benison, and Brahmanaspati, on him.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Firm is the sky and firm the earth, and steadfast also are these hills. Steadfast is all this living world, and steadfast is this King of men.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Steadfast, may Varuna the King, steadfast, the God Brhaspati, Steadfast, may Indra, steadfast too, may Agni keep thy steadfast reign.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: On constant Soma let us think with constant sacrificial gift And then may Indra make the clans bring tribute unto thee alone.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH offering for success in fight whence Indra was victorious. With this, O Brahmanaspati, let us attain to royal sway.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Subduing those who rival us, subduing all malignities, Withstand the man who menaces, withstand the man who angers us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Soma and Savitar the God have made thee a victorious King All elements have aided thee, to make thee general conqueror.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Oblation, that which Indra. gave and thus grew glorious and most high,- This have I offered, Gods! and hence now, verily, am rivalless.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Slayer of rivals, rivalless, victorious, with royal sway, Over these beings may I rule, may I be Sovran of the folk.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you according to the Law: Be harnessed to the shafts, and press.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Stones, drive calamity away, drive ye away malevolence: Make ye the Cows our medicine.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Of one accord the upper Stones, giving the Bull his bull-like strength, Look down with pride on those below.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Savitar the God, O Stones, stir you as Law commands for him Who sacrifices, pouring juice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: WITH hymns of praise their sons have told aloud the Rbhus' mighty deeds. Who, all-supporting, have enjoyed the earth as, twere a mother cow.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Bring forth the God with song divine, being Jatavedas hitherward, To bear our gifts at once to heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He here, a God-devoted Priest, led forward comes to sacrifice. Like a car covered for the road, he, glowing, knows, himself, the way.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: This Agni rescues from distress, as 'twere from the Immortal Race, A God yet mightier than strength, a God who hath been made for life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THE sapient with their spirit and their mind behold the Bird adorned with all an Asura's magic might. Sages observe him in the ocean's inmost depth: the wise disposers seek the station of his rays.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The flying Bird bears Speech within his spirit: erst the Gandharva in the womb pronounced it: And at the seat of sacrifice the sages cherish this radiant, heavenly-bright invention.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I saw the Herdsman, him who never resteth, approaching and departing on his pathways. He, clothed in gathered and diffusive splendour, within the worlds continually travels.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS very mighty one whom Gods commission, the Conqueror of cars, ever triumphant, Swift, fleet to battle, with uninjured fellies, even Tarksya for our weal will we call hither.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: As though we offered up our gifts to Indra, may we ascend. him as a ship. for safety. Like the two wide worlds, broad, deep far-extended, may we be safe both when he comes and leaves you.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: He who with might the Five Lands hath pervaded, like Surya with his lustre, and the waters- His strength wins hundreds, thousands none avert it, as the young maid repelleth not her lover.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now lift ye up yourselves and look on Indra's seasonable share. If it be ready, offer it; unready, ye have been remise.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Oblation is prepared: come to us, Indra; the Sun hath travelled over half his journey. Friends with their stores are sitting round thee waiting like lords of clans for the tribe's wandering chieftain.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dressed in the udder and on fire, I fancy; well-dressed, I fancy, is this recent present. Drink, Indra, of the curd of noon's libation with favour, Thunderer, thou whose deeds are mighty.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O MUCH-INVOKED, thou hast subdued thy foemen: thy might is loftiest; here display thy bounty. In thy right hand, O Indra, bring us treasures: thou art the Lord of rivers filled with riches.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Like a dread wild beast roaming on the mountain thou hast approached us from the farthest distance. Whetting thy bold and thy sharp blade, O Indra, crush thou the foe and scatter those who hate us.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou, mighty Indra, sprangest into being as strength for lovely lordship o'er the people. Thou drovest off the folk who were unfriendly, and to the Gods thou gavest room and freedom.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: VASISTHA mastered the Rathantara, took it from radiant Dhatar, Savitar, and Visnu, Oblation, portion of fourfold oblation, known by the names of Saprathas and Prathas.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: These sages found what lay remote and hidden, the sacrifice's loftiest secret essence. From radiant Dhatar, Savitar, and Visnu, from Agni, Bharadvaja brought the Brhat.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: They found with mental eyes the earliest Yajus, a pathway to the Gods, that had descended. From radiant Dhitar, Savitar, and Visnu, from Surya did these sages bring the Gharma.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: BRHASPATI lead us safely over troubless and turn his evil thought against the sinner; Repel the curse, and drive away ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort!
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May Naratarhsa aid us at Prayaja: blest be our Anuyaja at invokings. May he repel the curse, and chase ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: May he whose head is flaming burn the demons, haters of prayer, so that the arrow slay them. May he repel the curse and chase ill-feeling, and give the sacrificer peace and comfort.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I SAW thee meditating in thy spirit what sprang from Fervour and hath thence developed. Bestowing offspring here, bestowing riches, spread in thine offspring, thou who cravest children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I saw thee pondering in thine heart, and praying that in due time thy body might be fruitful. Come as a youthful woman, rise to meet me: spread in thine offspring, thou who cravest children.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: In plants and herbs, in all existent beings I have deposited the germ of increase. All progeny on earth have I engendered, and sons in women who will be hereafter.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: MAY Visnu form and mould the womb, may Tvastar duly shape the forms, Prajapati infuse the stream, and Dhatar lay the germ for thee.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O Sinivali, set the germ, set thou the germ, Sarasvati: May the Twain Gods bestow the germ, the Asvins crowned with lotuses.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: That which the Asvins Twain rub forth with the attrition-sticks of gold,- That germ of thine we invocate, that in the tenth month thou mayst bear.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: GREAT, unassailable must he the heavenly favour of' Three Gods, Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: O'er these, neither at home nor yet abroad or pathways that are Strange, The evil-minded foe hath power
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Nor over him, the man on whom the Sons of Aditi bestow Eternal light that he may live.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FILLING our hearts with health and joy, may Vata breathe his balm on us May he prolong our days of life.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Thou art our Father, Vata, yea, thou art a Brother and a friend, So give us strength that we may live.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The store of Amrta laid away yonder, O Vata, in thine home,- Give us thereof that we may live.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: To Agni send I forth my song, to him the Bull of all the folk: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who from the distance far away shines brilliantly across the wastes: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The Bull with brightly-gleaming flame who utterly consumes the fiends So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Who looks on all existing things and comprehends them with his view: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Resplendent Agni, who was born in farthest region of the air: So may he bear us past our foes.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Now send ye Jatavedas forth, send hitherward the vigorous Steed To seat him on our sacred grass.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: I raise the lofty eulogy of Jatavedas, raining boons, With sages for his hero band.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: With flames of Jatavedas which carry oblation to the Gods, May he promote our sacrifice.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THIS spotted Bull hath come, and sat before the Mother in the east, Advancing to his Father heaven.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Expiring when he draws his breath, she moves along the lucid spheres: The Bull shines out through all the sky.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Song is bestowed upon the Bird: it rules supreme through thirty realms Throughout the days at break of morn.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: FROM Fervour kindled to its height Eternal Law and Truth were born: Thence was the Night produced, and thence the billowy flood of sea arose.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: From that same billowy flood of sea the Year was afterwards produced, Ordainer of the days nights, Lord over all who close the eye.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Dhatar, the great Creator, then formed in due order Sun and Moon. He formed in order Heaven and Earth, the regions of the air, and light.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: THOU, mighty Agni, gatherest up all that is precious for thy friend. Bring us all treasures as thou art enkindled in libation's place
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: Assemble, speak together: let your minds be all of one accord, As ancient Gods unanimous sit down to their appointed share.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: The place is common, common the assembly, common the mind, so be their thought united. A common purpose do I lay before you, and worship with your general oblation.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary

verses.translation: One and the same be your resolve, and be your minds of one accord. United be the thoughts of all that all may happily agree.
verses.translationName: The Hymns of the Rigveda, translated with a popular commentary
